chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, elevating it to Muhammad ibn Faraj, who said:

I wrote to him asking about Abu Ali ibn Rashid, and Isa ibn Ja'far (ibn Asim), and Ibn Band. He wrote back to me: You mentioned Ibn Rashid, may Allah have mercy on him, for he lived a happy life and died a martyr. And he prayed for Ibn Band and the Asimi. Ibn Band was struck with a pillar and killed, and Ibn Asim was lashed with whips on the bridge three hundred times and thrown into the Tigris.
ai.seo_question: What was the fate of Ibn Rashid, Ibn Band, and Ibn Asim according to Imam al-Hadi (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the diverse modes of martyrdom (*shahada*) experienced by the Imam’s emissaries under Abbasid persecution, illustrating the concept of *saeed al-mawt* (happy death). It underscores the theological significance of their suffering as a means of spiritual elevation and divine witness, reinforcing the Shia understanding of martyrdom not merely as death, but as a blessed state of fidelity to the Imam.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 310 - Muhammad bin Yaqub has directly narrated from Muhammad bin Faraj that he said:

I wrote to Imam Hadi (a.s) asking about Ali bin Rashid, Isa bin Ja’far [bin Asim] and Ibn Band. Imam (a.s) wrote back: You have mentioned Ibn Rashid, who lived a righteous life and departed as a martyr. And they condemned Ibn Band and Asimi, but Ibn Band was clubbed to death and Ibn Asim was also lashed three hundred times on the Baghdad Bridge and thrown into the Tigris and he passed away.
